_comment: Disaster State Manager settings. PROTOTYPE values for software development only: none is an official Cauvery/Upper Anicut warning criterion and none has been hydrologically validated. Risk levels and rule IDs refer to the Risk Assessment Engine (config/risk_assessment.json). To adopt hydrologist-approved criteria, replace the 'conditions' and the persistence values in 'rules', record the approving authority and date in 'reference', and re-run tests/test_disaster_state_manager.py.
reference: Prototype assumptions (not approved by any authority).

conditions._comment: Each evaluation is classified into the FIRST condition it meets, in this order: EMERGENCY, ALERT, NORMAL, IMPROVED; otherwise ELEVATED. Invalid, stale, conflicting or indeterminate evidence is INSUFFICIENT and never meets any condition. river_threshold_min: the river reading itself must be at or above that CONFIGURED threshold (station threshold file: TEST values for the simulated station, never presented as official); when a station has no configured thresholds the requirement cannot be checked and the risk-based part applies alone. below_recovery_level: the river must be below the recovery level (warning level - river_thresholds.recovery_margin_m), so a level hovering just under the warning level is held by hysteresis instead of de-escalating.

river_thresholds._comment: Recovery level = configured warning level - recovery_margin_m. PROTOTYPE research/test value (hysteresis band), not an official CWC criterion.
river_thresholds.reference: Prototype hysteresis margin (not approved by any authority).

rules._comment: Per current state, rules are tried in order; the first whose condition holds AND whose persistence is met is the transition. Persistence counts DISTINCT observations (observed_at), never repeated evaluations of the same one. Escalation rules come first and ignore evaluation gaps; de-escalation rules require an unbroken run (gap_breaks_run). Sampling: an observation counts only if it is at least min_spacing_hours after the previously counted one (0.5 h, about half the hourly telemetry interval), and a de-escalation run ends where consecutive observations are more than max_gap_hours apart (3 h, the same as the river evidence's freshness limit max_age_hours). Escalation rules use max_gap_hours null so a worsening is never held back.

traffic._comment: PROTOTYPE recovery-exit requirement from the Traffic Agent (config/traffic_agent.json routes). Traffic NEVER escalates a state and never holds back an escalation. A rule with requires_traffic ROUTES_USABLE (only RECOVERY -> NORMAL here) is taken only when the latest TrafficAgent result has the same scope as the state record (simulated traffic can never change a real state), is at most max_age_hours old, and every configured evacuation route is in usable_route_conditions. Missing, stale, partial or wrong-scope traffic never counts as 'roads are fine': the state stays in RECOVERY. A BLOCKED route while the river looks normal is reported as CONFLICTING evidence. Without a TomTom key the live Traffic Agent returns DATA_UNAVAILABLE, so a real record cannot leave RECOVERY automatically.
